description: vsftpd 2.3.4 contains a backdoor triggered by a specific login string, allowing remote command execution.
FTP service exposed; credentials and data are transmitted in cleartext unless FTPS/SFTP is enforced.
Telnet is enabled; all traffic including credentials is unencrypted and susceptible to interception.
OpenSSH 7.2 is affected by a user enumeration vulnerability via timing differences during authentication.
SMTP service exposed to the network; verify open-relay configuration and enforce STARTTLS.
SMBv1 (port 445) may be vulnerable to the EternalBlue remote code execution exploit if unpatched.
NetBIOS session service exposed; can leak host/share information and enable enumeration attacks.
MySQL 5.5.x authentication bypass allowing repeated password guesses to eventually succeed due to a memcmp flaw.
Database service exposed directly to the network; should be restricted to application-tier hosts only.
RDP service exposed; if unpatched, vulnerable to BlueKeep pre-authentication remote code execution.
VNC service exposed; often configured with weak or no authentication, risking full remote desktop takeover.
Apache 2.2.x is vulnerable to the 'Range header' denial-of-service attack.
Unencrypted HTTP service exposed; consider redirecting to HTTPS.
HTTPS service exposed; confirm TLS configuration disables deprecated protocol versions and weak ciphers.
rpcbind exposure can be leveraged for UDP amplification denial-of-service attacks.
POP3 service exposed without TLS wrapper (use POP3S / port 995 instead).
